answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by making each identity costly: a newcomer must lock a refundable bond and earn endorsements from established peers. Picture the network as an orchard where every tree takes real effort to plant; one fake sapling is cheap, but a grove of credible identities costs stake, time, and reputation. Each claim is signed with a cipher key tied to that bond, and the nectar of rewards flows only to identities whose past work peers attested. Faking thousands of identities means thousands of bonds and checks, so the attack costs more than it earns.
